reviews.thm-short-five-lemma-in-an-abelian-categ: Reviewed against the repaired proof in Step 8 preflight. The monic half now chooses one common epic domain before taking the literal difference, carries that difference through row exactness and the two monic outer maps, and recovers equivalence of the original members. The epic half is the formal opposite-category dual, and balancedness supplies the isomorphism conclusion. Empty and zero objects remain covered by the short exact hypotheses.
reviews.thm-four-lemma-in-an-abelian-category: Reviewed against the repaired proof in Step 8 preflight. The risk is simultaneous compatibility of generalized-member equalities. Steps 1.2 and 2.1 now refine every relevant witness to one epic domain before subtraction, so the equations killed by p, gamma, or j-prime are literal on that domain. The remaining lifts use exactly the stated row exactness and outer monic or epic hypotheses.
reviews.thm-weak-four-lemma-with-the-exactness-h: Reviewed against the repaired proof in Step 8 preflight. The proof uses only exactness at X, Y, X-prime, and Y-prime, as claimed. Its two subtraction steps occur after simultaneous common-epic refinement, and the subsequent lifts use only the named monic and epic maps. No endpoint exactness or padded zero term is imported.
reviews.thm-nine-lemma-in-an-abelian-category: Reviewed against the repaired proof in Step 8 preflight. Step 1.1 obtains left exactness from the half-nine lemma. Step 2.1 proves the missing epicity directly: every required member equality is placed on one common epic refinement before the difference w is formed, column exactness lifts w, and monicity of the third column finishes. Step 3.1 applies this established implication in the opposite category for the reverse direction, so both directions of the iff are covered without the rejected endpoint-duality shortcut.
reviews.thm-nine-lemma-variants-by-which-rows-ar: Reviewed against the repaired proof in Step 8 preflight. The first two variants invoke the nine lemma with the appropriate pair of exact rows. For the middle-row variant, steps 1.3, 1.4, and 1.5 separately establish monicity, middle exactness, and epicity. The two differences are formed only after common epic refinement, preserving every zero-image and comparison equality used later.
reviews.thm-sharp-nine-lemma: Reviewed against the repaired proof in Step 8 preflight. Steps 1.1 and 1.2 use only exactness at the first two nodes of the columns and lower rows. The short-exact upgrade in step 2.1 uses the additional first-column and middle-row hypotheses only there, places all member equalities on one common epic domain before forming w, and proves the final top-row map epic without importing stronger assumptions.
